newsitem.title: UK: Astronomers find new mini-planet beyond Pluto.
newsitem.headline: Astronomers find new mini-planet beyond Pluto.

text.p: U.S. astronomers said on Wednesday they had discovered a new mini-planet, known as a planetesimal, orbiting at the edges of the solar system.
They said the as-yet unnamed object could represent a whole new class of orbiting chunks.
Jane Luu of the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics in Cambridge, Massachusetts and colleagues said the object, identified as 1996TL66, was 490 km in diameter and fairly massive.
Its highly elliptical orbit takes it within 35 Astronomical Units (AU) of the sun -- one AU being the distance the Earth is from the sun or 93 million miles (150 million km).
But its orbit goes out as far as 130 AU, far past the distant orbits of Pluto and Neptune.
About three dozen objects have been found in this region and are classified as members of the Kuiper belt. Even farther out is the Oort cloud, a group of comet-like objects.

"The discovery of this object in such a small fraction of the sky suggests that, unless we are improbably lucky, it is merely the first detected of a larger population of similar bodies," they wrote in a report in the science journal Nature.
